newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China activists petition over Japan isles row.
newsitem.headline: China activists petition over Japan isles row.

text.p: Political activists in southern China have collected 1,000 names on a cloth petition sheet, urging Beijing to put pressure on Japan over disputed islands in the East China Sea, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Monday.

Some 30 activists staged an hour-long signature collecting campaign on Sunday in Shenzhen, the south China city bordering Hong Kong, without being stopped by police, the Chinese-language Sing Tao Evening News said.
More than 1,000 people signed the petition on a two-by-three-metre cloth which was to be mailed to Chinese officials in the capital Beijing, it said.
They also handed out leaflets to passers-by, it said.
Chinese authorities usually prohibit demonstrations and have kept a tight lid on protests over the islands, which China calls the Diaoyus and Japan calls the Senkakus.

By contrast, anti-Japanese sentiment in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau has flared in recent months after Japanese right-wing activists erected a lighthouse and flags on the islands, located northeast of Taiwan.
Japan has claimed sovereignty over the islands since 1895, while China has claimed them for centuries.
